On physical examination, she has tenderness to palpation over the T7 vertebra, decreased strength in both lower extremities, and diminished sensation to light touch and pinprick from the T10 dermatome downwards.
Her reflexes are diminished in the lower extremities, and she has a positive Babinski sign bilaterally.
Bowel and bladder function are reported to be normal.
An urgent MRI of the thoracic spine reveals an epidural mass compressing the spinal cord at the T7 level.

She describes the pain as constant, worse at night, and not relieved by over-the-counter analgesics.
She also reports difficulty walking and has noticed a decreased sensation in her legs.
She denies any recent trauma or injury.
